Technical Architecture

8-Stage AI Governance Pipeline

From application request to audited AI response — every stage is policy-driven, deterministic, and machine-verifiable.

1

Application Request

The SaaS product, internal tool, or agentic workflow sends a chat/completion request through ANSARK instead of calling the LLM provider directly.

/v1/gateway/chattenant_idrequest_id
2

Identity & Rate Control

API key or JWT authentication is verified. Tenant scope is enforced, request IDs are propagated, and Redis-backed rate limits protect shared infrastructure.

API key / JWTtenant scopeRedis rate limit
3

Pre-LLM Safety Gates

Prompts are scanned for PII, jailbreak patterns, prompt injection attempts, and semantic risk. Redactions and blocks are logged as rule actions.

PII redactionjailbreak deny-listsemantic gate
4

Tenant Policy Resolution

The gateway loads tenant-specific signed policy configuration: rate limits, PII patterns, jailbreak rules, semantic settings, and numeric assertions.

policy YAMLHMAC signaturetenant config
5

Upstream LLM Call

Only approved and redacted prompts are forwarded to the model provider. Retries, timeouts, and circuit breaker state keep provider failures contained.

retry backofftimeout controlcircuit breaker
6

Response Validation

Model output is parsed and checked against expected JSON schemas and deterministic numeric assertions before it can return to the application.

JSON schemarate-card checksblock reason
7

Audit & Observability

Each decision produces structured actions and a hash-chained audit event. Metrics expose request counts, latency, block reasons, and dependency readiness.

PostgreSQL auditPrometheus metricsstructured logs
8

Governance Reporting

Security and compliance teams can retrieve tenant-level governance reports and trace runtime decisions back to policy versions and request IDs.

/v1/governance/reportpolicy versionblock reasons
